Compliance at Gemini is a team dedicated to managing the next generation of financial crime prevention in a complex and evolving regulatory environment. We are a diverse group of technology, legal, and operational professionals who develop new approaches to solving classic problems using cutting edge tools and processes.

The Role: Head of Consumer and Lending Compliance

In this role, you will lead the compliance program for Gemini’s deposit and lending products, including the first-in-class crypto rewards credit card and business credit card. You will be responsible for creating a comprehensive strategy to scale the program and support the business in delivering product features in a compliant and consumer-friendly way. The ideal candidate will have a deep knowledge of consumer finance regulations, be solutions-oriented, and have experience operating in a fast-moving environment. Superior communication skills are essential, as this individual will be required to communicate effectively with various stakeholders, including product, technology, legal, risk, as well as banking partners and regulators. Qualifications:

No Fault Litigation Attorney
OFFICE OF THE COMPTROLLER

The New York City Comptroller’s Office works to promote the financial health, integrity, and effectiveness of New York City government, in order to strengthen trust, secure a thriving future for all New Yorkers, and build a more just, equitable, and resilient city. Led by an independently elected citywide official, the comptroller’s office provides checks and balances needed to hold City government accountable for budgeting wisely, investing responsibly, operating efficiently, acting fairly, living up to its obligations and promises, and paying attention to the long-term challenges we face together.  Authorized by the New York City Charter, the Comptroller, through the Bureau of Law and Adjustment (BLA), negotiates and approves all monetary settlement of claims and lawsuits involving the City of New York. BLA investigates and, when in the best interest of the city, settles pre-litigation claims for and against the City of New York. In resolving claims before litigation is commenced, BLA protects the fiscal interest of the City while ensuring that pre-litigation claims are resolved in a fair and just manner, and in accordance with applicable laws. BLA furthers this goal in its review, evaluation, and authorization of requests to settle litigated cases involving the City and through diligent administration of disputes arising out of City contracts. BLA manages City risk by holding agencies accountable, rooting out fraud, and identifying trends, as well as, coordinating with the Law Department and other City agencies on issues that impact the public fiscal and public safety.  Under supervision of the Division Chief, No Fault Claims, with some latitude for independent judgment and unreviewed action and decision, performs legal work as the principal liaison attorney to the New York City Law Department on all First-Party and Third-Party litigation matters.  Duties include, but are not limited to the following:  • Serve as the principal litigation liaison attorney to the New York City Law Department on all First-Party and Third-Party litigation No-Fault matters; • Provide legal direction to the New York City Law Department on First-Party and Third-Party No-Fault litigation matters; • Serve as principal liaison attorney to the New York City Law Department, Office of NYC Comptroller Fiscal Services, and Marshal’s Office on all First-Party and Third Party No-Fault claims resulting in judgments and levies, including advising on the legally appropriate path to a legal and just disposition;  • When appropriate, negotiate and settle First-Party, Third Party, and Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist claims within delegated monetary authority level, prioritizing No-Fault litigation claims; • Manage Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist (UM claims from initial review through resolution, ensuring compliance with regulation 68; • Prepare UM cases for arbitration by analyzing supporting documentation, gathering evidence, and developing settlement and hearing strategies;                                                                                         • Respond to New York State Department of Financial Services correspondence; • Represent the City of New York in First-Party, Third-Party, and Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist arbitration proceedings; • Maintain accurate and complete claim files, prepare claim abstracts detailing the relevant information about the investigation and evaluation of liability and damages, document any events or conversations in claim notes, and upload documents upon receipt; • Maintain control over claim backlog, timely follow-up on requests made to agencies; • Investigate, identify, and report fraudulent claims, utilize statistical data to identify claims that pose potential risks, and provide risk management recommendations to the Division Chief; • Use available databases, media outlets, and other available sources to gather information relevant to the investigation of the claim; • Communicate effectively and professionally with other Comptroller staff, City agency employees, pro se claimants, and attorneys when investigating a claim or negotiating a settlement; and • Performs related assignments and special projects as required.

raw_text:
Deputy Director, Tort Unit
OFFICE OF THE COMPTROLLER

The New York City Comptroller’s Office works to promote the financial health, integrity, and effectiveness of New York City government, in order to strengthen trust, secure a thriving future for all New Yorkers, and build a more just, equitable, and resilient city. Led by an independently elected citywide official, the comptroller’s office provides checks and balances needed to hold City government accountable for budgeting wisely, investing responsibly, operating efficiently, acting fairly, living up to its obligations and promises, and paying attention to the long-term challenges we face together.  Authorized by the New York City Charter, the Comptroller, through the Bureau of Law and Adjustment (BLA), negotiates and approves all monetary settlement of claims and lawsuits involving the City of New York. BLA investigates and, when in the best interest of the city, settles pre-litigation claims for and against the City of New York. In resolving claims before litigation is commenced, BLA protects the fiscal interest of the City while ensuring that pre-litigation claims are resolved in a fair and just manner, and in accordance with applicable laws. BLA furthers this goal in its review, evaluation, and authorization of requests to settle litigated cases involving the City and through diligent administration of disputes arising out of City contracts. BLA manages City risk by holding agencies accountable, rooting out fraud, and identifying trends, as well as, coordinating with the Law Department and other City agencies on issues that impact the public fiscal and public safety.  The Deputy Director, Tort Unit reports directly to the Director, Tort Unit, under the general direction of the Assistant Comptroller for the Bureau of Law and Adjustment. Duties and responsibilities of the position include, but are not limited to the following:  • Advise and assist the Director in managing and directing all functions of the Tort Unit, including overseeing the day-to-day operations, and in the Director’s absence, perform the Director’s duties; • Supervise all Tort Division Chiefs and Claim Examiners and ensure duties are performed in accordance with the highest professional standards; manage the pre-litigation settlement process of tort claims and the 50h process, ensure the proper handling of no-fault claims and affirmative property damage claims and managing claim support;   • Assist the Director in bureau-wide operational projects and managing the procurement of Bureau professional services such as the Statutory 50-h contract and the purchasing of those services;  • Monitor high-profile and high-exposure claims and perform legal research and draft memoranda on critical issues affecting pre-litigation claims; delegate within independent authority and with discretion, appropriate monetary settlement authority to Tort Division staff; • Resolve claim payment issues including coordinating with Office of General Counsel on lien issues and serving as one of the principal liaisons between the Bureau of Law & Adjustment and the Office of Fiscal Services; assist in the managing of the Son of Sam process including coordinating with the NYS Office of Attorney General; • Coordinating with the FOIL Officer, Press Office and Community Action Center to respond to requests for information which includes validation of reports and information; • Identify trends and changes in municipal litigation, including recent case law developments, and provide relevant recommendations to the Director, Assistant Comptroller, and other executive staff;  • Assist BLA units in liability and damages evaluation; provide efficient and effective risk management assessment strategies and recommendations with respect to claims filed against various City agencies;  • Handle administrative matters, including but not limited to, data/technology, human resources, and any other administrative issues assigned by the Director; assist the Director in the annual staff evaluations in accordance with human resources protocol; develop and present professional development and legal training to new and existing staff; and,  • Perform all other duties as requested by the Director and Assistant Comptroller as needed.

Director, Organic Growth & Discoverability
Brex — San Francisco, California, United States

Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Growth Marketing at Brex

Growth Marketing is Brex’s pipeline engine. We own paid acquisition, organic and SEO, lifecycle marketing, events and field marketing, partner marketing, and marketing operations. We carry a number: SQL ARR, bookings, and self-serve activations. Every function on the team is accountable to it. 

We run lean. We pair small teams with AI and automation instead of scaling headcount. Our marketing ops team uses Claude, Clay, and custom integrations to do work that used to require twice as many people. Our paid team manages eight figures of annual spend with four people. 

We work closely with sales, SDR leadership, engineering, and design. We own top-of-funnel through meeting creation. We push back when the data says something different than the room expects. And we’re building with startup speed and a much larger balance sheet behind us. 

What you’ll do

Brex’s buyers find and evaluate us across a growing set of surfaces: Google, AI answer engines, Reddit, G2, YouTube. No single person owns visibility across all of them today. You will.

As Director of Organic Growth & Discoverability, you’ll own everything between paid acquisition and brand that drives a buyer from first discovery to qualified lead. You set the strategy, build the team, decide how we work with agencies, and carry the number. You report to the Head of Growth Marketing.

This is what we expect in the first 12–18 months:

- Grow qualified organic traffic and improve conversion from organic visitors to activated users and pipeline.

- Move Brex’s share of voice in AI-generated answers for corporate cards, expense management, and business banking. Stand up the tracking to know if you’re winning.

- Recover and surpass keyword positions lost to competitors in recent algorithm shifts.

- Stand up a content production engine that ships work that ranks, without every piece needing a senior review.

- Cut the vendor stack down. Make what’s left accountable and tell us what should move in-house.

- Hire and develop the team. You'll inherit some of it, grow it from there, and set the editorial, technical, and AI-native bar for the work.

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in our San Francisco office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three days per week in office - Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Responsibilities

- Set the organic growth strategy and own the roadmap, OKRs, and budget. You’re accountable for how Brex shows up organically.

- Build Brex’s AEO/GEO playbook. Own how Brex shows up in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, and Google AI Overviews: citation strategy, content structured for model retrieval, and the tracking to tell us what’s moving.

- Co-own the technical SEO roadmap with web engineering: site architecture, Core Web Vitals, schema, crawl, page performance. Translate SEO needs into specs engineers can ship.

- Run content strategy and production for organic. Set the editorial bar, own the calendar, and build a production process that doesn’t bottleneck on you.

- Unify our presence across Reddit, G2, YouTube, and other community and review surfaces into one discoverability strategy instead of a collection of side projects.

- Get sales and partnerships up to speed on how organic and AI search are changing, and what that means when they’re in a competitive deal.

- Be a culture carrier for the Growth Marketing team. Model the AI-native, high-ownership way of working we're building toward.

Requirements

- Experience: 8+ years in SEO, organic growth, or digital marketing, with at least 3 years leading a team and owning strategy and budget at a B2B SaaS, fintech, or technology company.

- Pipeline orientation: You connect organic channels to pipeline, revenue, and business outcomes, not just traffic and rankings. You think in SQLs, activation rates, and CAC efficiency.

- Technical SEO depth: You can read crawl logs, diagnose Core Web Vitals issues, direct schema implementations, and partner credibly with engineers on site architecture decisions.

- AI visibility fluency: You’ve actively experimented with citation strategies, structured content for model consumption, or measured share of voice in answer engines. We can’t train this on the job.

- Content instincts: You can tell the difference between content that earns trust and content that fills a page. You have experience building or managing content operations at scale with high editorial standards.

- Vendor management judgment: You’ve managed agencies and know how to hold them to outcomes, not just deliverables. You also know when to stop outsourcing and bring work in-house.

- Comfort with ambiguity: You make consequential decisions with incomplete data. You like building a function from scratch more than running one that’s already humming.

- Experimentation mindset: You treat failure as a feedback loop. You run experiments, kill what doesn’t work quickly, and double down on what does.

Bonus points

- You’ve navigated a major Google algorithm update that materially impacted your business and can walk through how you diagnosed, adapted, and recovered.

- You understand how retrieval-augmented generation systems select and rank sources, and you can translate that into actionable content and structural strategy.

- You use AI and automation tools in your own workflows. You’re a practitioner, not just a strategist.

- Experience in a regulated or compliance-sensitive industry.

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $220,000 - $276,000. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors, including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

Brex LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary of Capital One, N.A.
Please be aware, job-seekers may be at risk of targeting by malicious actors looking for personal data. Brex recruiters will only reach out via LinkedIn or email with a brex.com domain. Any outreach claiming to be from Brex via other sources should be ignored.

2027 Point72 Academy Investment Analyst Summer Internship Program - Hong Kong
Point72 — Hong Kong

The Point72 Academy Summer Internship — Hong Kong

Are you a student interested in pursuing a career in investing? If you are graduating between December 2027 and July 2028, we invite you to apply for our 8-week summer internship, taking place from June to August 2027.   

Launch your investing career in the Point72 Academy, an investment analyst training program that will provide you with the tools and knowledge to build a career in our ever-evolving industry. Since 2015, the Academy has graduated more than 230 analysts onto our platform as of November 2025; some are portfolio managers today.   

The Point72 Academy Summer Internship is a combination of classroom instruction, portfolio casework, and mentorship. The program is designed to give you insights into finance, research, and the workings of the public markets and prepare you for a potential opportunity with the full-time Point72 Academy Associate Program.

 

During the internship, you will:   

- Acquire fundamental knowledge and skills necessary to contribute as an analyst, alongside your peers.

- Receive training in accounting, modeling, presenting, and compliance.

- Collaborate with an investment team, gaining firsthand experience of the daily life of an equities analyst and exposure to one of the sectors covered by our Portfolio Managers.

- Work closely with Academy coaches, delving deeper into data analysis and preparing a final pitch on an investment idea.

- Collaborate with Compliance, Information Security and the Office of the Co-CIO to discover efficient ways to harness AI in your investment processes and workflows

 

Who We’re Looking For: 

- We welcome students from all academic disciplines. Your field of study or major is not a determining factor; we seek individuals who can effectively manage teamwork, exhibit integrity, possess intellectual curiosity, demonstrate leadership potential, and express a keen interest in the financial markets.

- Students should have a high enthusiasm for the financial services industry. Interest in analyzing companies and looking at stocks is recommended given the project-based nature of this program.

- Highly self‑motivated with a high risk appetite and the ability to make decisions in an ambiguous environment.

- Candidates with excellent communication skills, both written and verbal in an Asian language.

 

We Want You to Apply if You Are: 

- A current student who will graduate from university between December 2027 and July 2028.

- Fascinated by research and problem-solving, relentlessly curious, and constantly expanding your horizons.

- Committed to continued success in your academic and professional career with the highest levels of professionalism, integrity, and excellence.

- Commitment to the highest ethical standards.

- Highly self-driven and motivated to explore a career in finance. 

 

What to Expect: 

- Your online application, essays, and resume will serve as an introduction to who you are as a candidate. Once you complete the online application, we will begin reviewing your profile. 

- Selected candidates will then receive an email invitation to participate in a case study, allowing you to showcase your experiences and demonstrate your business acumen.   

- Following submission and review of your case study, shortlisted candidates will be invited to complete an online assessment and participate in virtual one‑on‑one interviews with various members of the Academy team. Shortlisted candidates will then be invited to attend a half‑day assessment center. There are two application deadlines: one in mid‑May for candidates interested in an early summer assessment center, and another for students applying over the summer to mid Fall, which will lead to a late fall assessment center. We strongly encourage candidates to apply and complete all requirements as soon as they feel ready to begin the hiring process.

 

Please note, you may only submit one application to the Academy internship program globally, so only apply to the region you are most interested in.

Don't miss this opportunity to kickstart your career in the world of investing with the Point72 Academy.   

Please note that any use of GenAI is strictly prohibited when completing this application.  

 

ABOUT POINT72 

Point72 is a leading global alternative investment firm led by Steven A. Cohen. Building on more than 30 years of investing experience, Point72 seeks to deliver superior returns for its investors through fundamental and systematic investing strategies across asset classes and geographies. We aim to attract and retain the industry’s brightest talent by cultivating an investor-led culture and committing to our people’s long-term growth.

We’re a firm that thrives on ideas, and we’ve found that the Point72 Academy has provided us with diverse viewpoints and perspectives, and we are able to offer support in their growth and development as analysts and portfolio managers.

Associate Director of Product Design
CAMPAIGN FINANCE BOARD

ABOUT THE CAMPAIGN FINANCE BOARD   The Campaign Finance Board is a nonpartisan, independent city agency that empowers New Yorkers to have a greater impact on their elections. Our mission is to make local democracy more open, transparent, and equitable by removing barriers to participation.   We make it easier for New Yorkers to vote, meaningfully support candidates for city office, and run for office themselves. NYC Votes, our voter engagement initiative, meets people where they are to share trustworthy election information and help New Yorkers make a plan to vote. We publish the citywide Voter Guide, which delivers information about candidates directly to voters’ doors. Our public matching funds program ensures small contributions can make a big difference, allowing regular people to run for office by relying on the support of other regular people, not just wealthy donors and special interests. And we lift the veil on how candidates raise and spend money, increasing transparency and accountability in local government.   We believe that when every New Yorker is empowered to participate meaningfully in elections, candidates will better reflect the communities they serve, elected leaders will be more accountable to the public, and New Yorkers will have a democracy they can truly trust.   ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT    The Strategy, Products, and Innovation division is the agency’s newest division and leads the strategic planning and policy work, working across the agency to test out and implement new ideas. This division also creates and actions on the agency’s product roadmap to take us into future elections while maintaining and improving existing systems. The new Product Strategy vertical will be responsible for creating the overall roadmap for tech modernization and process improvements; prioritize tech projects to pursue, and liaise between technical engineers and subject matter experts; and align tech projects with the agency’s strategic plan and objectives. Plans for this vertical include building new teams for product management as well as user experience and service design, as well as some reorganization of existing PMO functions.   JOB DESCRIPTION    The Associate Director of Product Design is a senior design leader responsible for driving the execution of user-centered design across digital products and public-facing services. Reporting to the Senior Director of Product, this role translates high-level design vision into actionable product experiences that improve service delivery, accessibility, and trust in government. The Associate Director of Product Design plays a critical role in embedding human-centered design practices into cross-functional teams, ensuring that policy-driven requirements are transformed into intuitive, equitable, and accessible digital experiences. This leader balances strategy and hands-on design oversight, mentoring designers while partnering closely with product and engineering leadership.   Unlike private sector roles focused on revenue or growth metrics, success in this role is measured by usability, accessibility, adoption, clarity, and public value.   This position will require the selected candidate to obtain NYC residency within 90 days of starting their job and be in-person in the CFB Manhattan office a minimum of 1 day a week.   Responsibilities include but are not limited to:      -  Lead end-to-end product design efforts for key digital services and platforms.     -  Translate policy, operational, and regulatory requirements into simple, intuitive user experiences.     -  Ensure consistent application of design standards, accessibility requirements, and inclusive design principles.     -  Oversee user flows, interaction models, wireframes, prototypes, and high-fidelity design outputs.     -  Champion user research practices including interviews, usability testing, journey mapping, and accessibility testing.     -  Ensure all digital products meet accessibility standards (Section 508, WCAG).     -  Embed inclusive design practices that account for language access, digital literacy, disability access, and device constraints.     -  Promote scalable, modular design practices across products.     -  Serve as an advocate for human-centered design within the agency, helping non-design teams understand and adopt iterative, user-focused workflows.     -  Mentor and coach mid-level and senior designers, providing feedback and growth opportunities while supporting hiring efforts to build a diverse, high-performing design team.     -  Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and mission-driven team culture. Knowledge     -  Comprehensive understanding of human-centered design, including user research, interaction design, usability testing, and service design.     -  Deep knowledge of accessibility standards such as WCAG, Section 508, and ADA considerations.     -  Familiarity with digital product development lifecycles, specifically agile and iterative delivery practices.     -  Expertise in design systems, component libraries, and scalable interface patterns.     -  Understanding of frontend implementation, including responsive design and interaction behaviors.     -  Solid grounding in inclusive and equity-centered design principles.     -  Understanding of data-informed design and the use of usability metrics.    Skills     -  Ability to simplify complex processes and policy-driven workflows through high-quality design.     -  Proficiency in planning and conducting user research and translating findings into actionable improvements.     -  Skill in defining and tracking design quality metrics, such as usability scores, task completion rates, and accessibility audit pass rates.     -  Strong skills in leading workshops, stakeholder alignment sessions, and design critiques.     -  Skill in facilitating co-design sessions with end users, specifically those from underserved or historically excluded communities.     -  Demonstrated ability to navigate and find "middle ground" when policy-driven requirements conflict with user experience.     -  Mastery of modern design tools, specifically Figma or comparable platforms.     -  Strong written and verbal skills, with the ability to present design rationale to non-technical stakeholders.     -  Proven ability to work across cross-functional teams, including product, engineering, policy, and communications.     -   Effective mentorship and people management skills, with a focus on developing staff for career growth.    Abilities     -  Build consensus for design decisions among leadership, legal, and policy teams.     -  Create clear design specifications, documentation, and reusable patterns.     -  Build structure and processes within forming teams or organizational uncertainty.     -  Translate design impact into mission-driven language for executive audiences.     -  Lead end-to-end design initiatives from concept through implementation and iteration.     -  Remain flexible and adjust plans while working effectively under pressure.     -  Balance high-level strategic thinking with hands-on design execution.     -  Build trust with diverse internal teams and external communities.     -  Demonstrated ability as a creative problem solver. This includes the daily management of the Offices of Financial Management, Purchasing and Contracts, Operational Services, and Diversity and Inclusion.  The Office of Purchasing and Contracts serves as the central procurement unit entrusted with overseeing the procurement of goods and services on behalf of the Department of Finance. This office handles the management of the department’s current contract portfolio, including the vital responsibility of ensuring compliance with DOF’s Minority and Woman-Owned Enterprise (M/WBE) program in accordance with the requirements of New York State Law, the New York City Charter, the Administrative Code of the City of New York, and Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules. raw_text:
Business Systems Architect, GTM Systems
Betterment — Betterment HQ - New York City

About Betterment

Betterment is a leading, technology-driven financial services company that offers investing, savings and retirement solutions for retail investors and investment advisors as well as financial wellness solutions, including a 401(k) for small and medium-sized businesses. Our team is passionate about our mission, to empower people to build wealth with confidence and ease. We’re headquartered in NYC and offer hybrid NY-based positions (four days/ week in-office, with no required office days during the summer and winter holidays).

About the Role

We’re looking for a senior individual contributor to own the architecture and ongoing health of Betterment’s GTM systems ecosystem, with Salesforce at the center and a growing set of surrounding integrations.

This is a staff-level technical leadership role for someone who wants to spend their time solving hard systems problems, setting technical direction, and raising the bar for how our GTM systems are built.

This role goes well beyond system administration or ticket fulfillment. As the staff-level architect for Betterment’s GTM systems ecosystem, you’ll define technical direction across our stack, proactively identify architectural risks and opportunities, and bring forward new approaches before they become stakeholder asks.

You’ll partner closely with our Sales, Betterment Advisor Solutions (BAS), and Betterment at Work (B@W) teams as the primary technical counterpart to their workflows, and collaborate with our Data and Product/Engineering organizations on systems integration and data integrity. You’ll guide how our tools work together - Salesforce, HubSpot, Clay, and the rest of our GTM stack - and ensure we’re building for long-term scalability, data quality, and business impact.

This role is not the primary owner of routine system administration, basic ticket fulfillment, or standard stakeholder intake; it is focused on the most complex architectural, integration, and platform-health problems across our GTM systems.

You’ll be a force multiplier for the broader Business Systems & Tools team: reviewing solution designs, mentoring engineers on architecture and integration patterns, and stepping into the team’s highest-risk or most ambiguous cross-system work to unblock progress and raise the quality bar.

This role is based out of our NYC office. Below we've reflected the base salary range for this position. Actual salaries may vary depending on factors including but not limited to location, experience, and performance. The range listed is just one component of Betterment’s total compensation package for employees. 

- New York City: $155,000- $175,000

This job may also be eligible for variable compensation in the form of a company incentive bonus. 

A Day in the Life

Own the GTM systems architecture

- Define and maintain the target architecture for our GTM systems ecosystem - how data and workflows should move between Salesforce, HubSpot, Clay, and adjacent tools such as enrichment, engagement, telephony, billing, and analytics - and drive the stack toward it.

- Define and maintain the canonical GTM systems architecture, including system-of-record boundaries, key data domains, integration patterns, and architecture decision records, so the team has clear standards to build against.

- Design and build scalable, maintainable solutions for our most complex, cross-system initiatives, owning them from problem framing through deployment.

- Continuously audit the health of the stack: integration reliability, data integrity, technical debt, security posture, permissions, auditability, and platform limits - and drive remediation before problems reach stakeholders.

Set technical direction and raise the bar

- Review and guide solution designs across the Business Systems & Tools team, providing guardrails and feedback that improve scalability, maintainability, and clarity.

- Establish and evangelize standards for integration patterns, data design, deployment practices, release governance, and documentation.

- Mentor engineers on architecture and technical decision-making, leading through influence and expertise rather than direct management.

Act as the primary technical counterpart to GTM teams

- Partner with Sales, BAS, and B@W stakeholders to deeply understand their workflows, frame problems, evaluate tradeoffs, and translate needs into pragmatic system designs.

- Serve as the resident thought leader on GTM systems: track where the market is going, especially in AI-driven GTM tooling and data enrichment, proactively bring stakeholders new approaches, and pressure-test vendor claims against real requirements.

- Collaborate with Data and Product/Engineering teams on systems integration, data contracts, and data integrity across the company’s platforms.

Lead the hardest cross-system work

- Step into the highest-priority or highest-risk initiatives across stakeholder areas when deep architectural ownership is needed, especially when work spans multiple tools, teams, or business processes.

- Lead the technical diligence and implementation architecture for new tools and major platform changes: define requirements, assess fit against our target architecture, coordinate security and integration design, and guide implementation through UAT and cutover.

What We’re Looking For

Architecture & Systems Depth

- Deep expertise with Salesforce as the core system of record for GTM, including declarative, programmatic, and integration approaches - and, more importantly, the architectural judgment to choose the right pattern based on scale, maintainability, risk, and downstream data implications.

- Demonstrated experience owning architecture for a multi-tool GTM stack in a B2B or SaaS environment: designing integrations, defining data flows, and managing system dependencies at scale.

- Strong understanding of integration design patterns such as APIs, middleware, and event-driven flows, and their implications for reliability, reporting, user experience, and operational support.

- Experience with marketing automation and sales engagement platforms, with HubSpot strongly preferred, and with GTM data enrichment/orchestration tooling; experience with Clay or similar signal-based automation platforms is a significant plus.

- Solid data literacy: comfortable defining data contracts, validating data across systems, and partnering with data and analytics teams on integrity and reporting.

- Strong judgment on permissions, auditability, release risk, and data governance in complex business systems environments.

Technical Leadership

- A track record of operating as a staff-level or lead IC: setting technical direction, reviewing others’ designs, and raising quality across a team without formal management authority.

- Proven ability to own ambiguous, high-stakes projects end-to-end, from problem discovery through deployment and adoption, with minimal oversight.

- Experience defining durable architecture artifacts and operating mechanisms, not just delivering projects.

- Experience running or heavily contributing to vendor evaluations and platform migrations, including technical diligence, security considerations, and implementation planning.

Consultative Partnership

- Strong consultative mindset - you ask the right questions, challenge assumptions, make tradeoffs transparent, and co-create solutions with stakeholders in ambiguous environments.

- Proven ability to build trust with GTM leaders and represent systems thinking in cross-functional forums, translating between technical and business audiences fluently.

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills - clear documentation, crisp design docs, and skimmable stakeholder updates.

Nice to Have

- Salesforce architect-track certifications such as Application Architect, System Architect, or Integration Architecture Designer.

- Experience with AI-driven GTM workflows, including automated enrichment, outbound orchestration, or conversation intelligence writing back to CRM.

- Experience with deployment and DevOps tooling for Salesforce, such as Copado, and release management best practices.

- Familiarity with the broader RevOps stack, including call intelligence, sales engagement, customer success platforms, billing, and BI tools.

Join a team built on these core values

We change lives

Be a part of a community of innovators working to transform financial outcomes for real people. Your work will make an impact, always laddering up to our mission; to empower people to build wealth with confidence and ease.

We set audacious goals

We set them for the company, our customers, and ourselves, and we won’t stop until we reach them. We don’t just show up; we give our all, then celebrate our wins.

We value all perspectives

When we collaborate, we're at our best. We believe diverse perspectives lead to better outcomes and strive to uphold our supportive and inclusive community.

We simplify financial services

We’re financial services pioneers, always finding new ways to improve, optimize, and enhance. Constant improvement is in our DNA.

 Our Commitment to Your Total Well-being:

- We offer a competitive suite of benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage; life and AD&D insurance; short- and long-term disability; infertility support and WPATH-aligned transgender health benefits; an Employee Assistance Program (EAP); transit benefits and FSA and HSA options

- Ownership: Equity for all employees, including new hire and refresher grants.

- Time: Flexible paid time off, paid parental leave, and a fully paid four-week sabbatical in your sixth year.

- Growth: Company-paid professional coaching for all employees.

- Wealth: Day-one 401(k) match plus matching on qualified student loan payments.

What happens next

We’ll take a few weeks to review all applications. If we’d like to spend more time with you, we’ll reach out to arrange next steps, which will include 3-4 sets of meetings with your future colleagues.

In the interview process, we’ll look to learn more about your skills, experiences, capabilities, and motivators. Many of our questions will be aimed at understanding how you might operate here at Betterment. Depending on the role, we may ask you to complete a case study exercise or technical assessments, as we want to collect a robust set of data points to better inform our decisions.

On average, it takes us around 3-5 weeks to make a hiring decision, depending on your availability and sense of urgency. As a best practice, we aim to interview at least 2-3 final round candidates before making a hiring decision. Please note that, as we usually receive an overwhelming number of applications for open positions, we’re unable to offer individual feedback during the interview process. 

We recognize that interviewing for a new role is a big deal. We appreciate you considering Betterment as the next step in your career, and our Recruiting Team is here to support and advocate for you through the interview process!

Betterment is dedicated to providing accommodations to candidates upon request. If you need accommodations at any point throughout the interview process, please reach out to your recruiter. 

Please note that in any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.

Come join us! 

We’re an equal opportunity employer and comply with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. We strictly prohibit and do not tolerate discrimination against employees, applicants, or any other covered persons because of race, color, religion, creed, national origin or ancestry, ethnicity, sex, gender (including gender nonconformity and status as a transgender or transsexual individual),

Senior Attorney, litigation
OFFICE OF THE COMPTROLLER

The New York City Comptroller’s Office works to promote the financial health, integrity, and effectiveness of New York City government, in order to strengthen trust, secure a thriving future for all New Yorkers, and build a more just, equitable, and resilient city. Led by an independently elected citywide official, the comptroller’s office provides checks and balances needed to hold City government accountable for budgeting wisely, investing responsibly, operating efficiently, acting fairly, living up to its obligations and promises, and paying attention to the long-term challenges we face together.  Authorized by the New York City Charter, the Comptroller, through the Bureau of Law and Adjustment (BLA), negotiates and approves all monetary settlement of claims and lawsuits involving the City of New York. BLA investigates and, when in the best interest of the city, settles pre-litigation claims for and against the City of New York. In resolving claims before litigation is commenced, BLA protects the fiscal interest of the City while ensuring that pre-litigation claims are resolved in a fair and just manner, and in accordance with applicable laws. BLA furthers this goal in its review, evaluation, and authorization of requests to settle litigated cases involving the City and through diligent administration of disputes arising out of City contracts. BLA manages City risk by holding agencies accountable, rooting out fraud, and identifying trends, as well as, coordinating with the Law Department and other City agencies on issues that impact the public fiscal and public safety.  Reporting directly to the Deputy Director of Litigation, duties for the Senior Attorney position include, but are not limited to, the following:  •	Using independent judgment and applying appropriate standards of law:   1. He paired Stravinsky with Picasso, Coco Chanel with choreographers, composers with painters. He wasn’t the person on stage, but he created the conditions that made extraordinary work possible. Every production demanded creative ambition, difficult tradeoffs, relentless coordination, and uncompromising standards. 

Great creative production feels a lot like that.

You’ll lead production across our most ambitious campaigns and projects while building the systems and external network that allow exceptional creative work to happen again and again.

You see production as a creative discipline. You know how to protect bold ideas, challenge underdeveloped briefs, make difficult tradeoffs, and bring clarity to complexity. This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who wants to build the function while still personally producing our biggest creative bets.

In this role, you’ll:

- Establish how Brand Creative prioritizes, staffs, greenlights, reviews, and delivers projects, creating a production system that makes exceptional work more repeatable.

- Bring clarity to complex projects by keeping creative leaders and cross-functional partners grounded in the real state of the work, decisions, constraints, tradeoffs, and risks.

- Work directly with Brand Creative leadership to continually raise the quality of the work and build one of the strongest in-house creative teams in the industry.

What you’ll bring:

- Significant experience leading complex, multidisciplinary creative production, with a track record of independently owning large-scale campaigns and multiple concurrent creative projects.

- Deep production experience across film, photography, motion, experiential, digital, and integrated brand work, with the judgment to choose the right production model for the idea.

- Strong financial and operational judgment, including experience with scoping, staffing, budgeting, forecasting, and managing meaningful production investments.

- A track record of building production systems, capabilities, or ways of working, not simply operating within established ones.

In addition to the learning and development you'll receive in your day-to-day role with your team, as part of our summer internship program you will:

- Work alongside your fellow interns and be mentored by experienced professionals

- Meet your peers through designated intern programming, volunteer opportunities, and social events

- Attend sessions with senior leaders discussing their expertise and career paths

- Have hands-on access to best-in-class tools and resources

- Gain exposure to groups and functions with unique responsibilities and perspectives on our industry

- Develop your technical, writing, and presentation skills

 

When you apply to our internship program, you will be considered for a variety of teams based on your interests and experience and our business needs. 

 

What's Required

- Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree

- Interest in the asset management industry

- Ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines in a fast-paced environment

- Strong attention to detail

- Strong analytical, writing, verbal communication, and technical skills

- Demonstrated ability to work cooperatively with all levels of the team

- Demonstrate professionalism and integrity in all interactions

- Commitment to the highest ethical standards

 

Team Overviews

Communications

The Corporate Communications team manages the global reputation of Point72 across media relations, external and internal communications, digital content, and brand management. Interns gain exposure to research and content creation - including media monitoring, competitive audits, branded recruiting and digital content, event planning, and bespoke projects - working closely with senior management and functional leaders firmwide.

Compliance

The Compliance team supports the firm's global investment and trading activities by establishing and enforcing the firm’s compliance policies, providing real-time advice, and conducting pre- and post-trade surveillance. Interns will gain exposure to enforcing the Code of Ethics and personal trading programs, liaising with global regulators, maintaining the firm's restricted list, and performing due diligence on research providers, consultants, and trading counterparties.

Finance

The Corporate Finance team provides timely, accurate financial information, advice, and services to business partners across Corporate Accounting, Global Payments, Procurement, FP&A, and Financial Reporting. Interns will gain exposure to day-to-day activities such as the month-end close, investor risk reports, and consolidated monthly financial packages, while sharpening Excel, writing, and presentation skills through intensive mentoring.

Operations

The Trade Support team, part of Operations, supports the operational aspects of trade processing, reconciliation, financing, and reporting for all products across global markets - equities, derivatives, bonds, foreign exchange, and futures. Interns will gain exposure to working with traders and counterparties to resolve trading matters and help provide accurate books and records for the firm on a daily and monthly basis.

Strategic Implementation

The Strategic Implementation team leads complex, cross-functional initiatives that support the growth of Point72's businesses, partnering with Strategy, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Operations, and Technology. Interns will gain exposure to the end-to-end program cycle —

coordinating meetings and deliverables, building project plans and timelines, documenting current state, conducting root cause analysis, and developing playbooks for key activities.

Strategy

The Corporate Strategy team is a small, multidisciplinary group reporting to the Chief Operating Officer that identifies, designs, and executes value-creating cross-functional initiatives and engages in new business and special situations. Interns will gain exposure to strategic priorities by supporting analyses on operations, performing quantitative and qualitative research (competitive analysis, industry trends, market conditions), and providing project management support on key initiatives.

Regulatory Reporting

The Regulatory Reporting team provides governance across all regulatory filings and obligations globally, including submissions to the SEC, CFTC, NFA, MAS, FCA, SFC, and Kanto Finance Bureau. Interns will gain exposure to filing preparation and submission, execute data reconciliations and exception investigations, partner with Compliance, Legal, Finance, Risk, Technology, and Trading, and help identify automation opportunities that improve accuracy and reduce manual effort.

Treasury

The Treasury team supports the firm's credit and treasury functions across Central Funding, Securities Lending, and Broker Relations—verifying and disputing margin calls, reporting on counterparty exposure, investing excess cash, and negotiating margin terms with prime brokers and derivative counterparts. Interns will gain hands-on exposure to a wide range of financial instruments across global markets while working alongside senior treasury professionals.

Human Capital

The Human Capital team serves as trusted business partners and advisors within the Point72 community, committed to driving a distinctive culture that values collaboration, innovation, and adaptive performance. Interns will gain exposure to day-to-day HR operations including onboarding, employee records, and benefits administration, along with recruiting and interview coordination, HR reporting and project work, and compliance and privacy best practices for handling confidential information.

Legal

The Legal team works to deliver exceptional legal services in a manner that promotes the firm’s performance with the utmost integrity and supports all Point72 groups globally with practical advice on a variety of complex legal and regulatory matters in an ever-changing, dynamic environment. Interns will gain exposure to regulatory filings and obligations, drafting and updating firm policies, due diligence reviews, and industry best-in-class automation and data visualization tools that support the department.

About Point72

Point72 is a leading global alternative investment firm led by Steven A. Cohen. Building on more than 30 years of investing experience, Point72 seeks to deliver superior returns for its investors through fundamental and systematic investing strategies across asset classes and geographies. We aim to attract and retain the industry's brightest talent by cultivating an investor-led culture and committing to our people's long-term growth. For more information, visit https://point72.com/.

The annual base salary is $75,000 (USD) which will be prorated based on internship start and end date. Actual compensation offered to the successful candidate may vary from posted hiring based upon geographic location, work experience, education, and/or skill level, among other things.

Senior Director of Engineering
CAMPAIGN FINANCE BOARD

ABOUT THE CAMPAIGN FINANCE BOARD    The Campaign Finance Board is a nonpartisan, independent city agency that empowers New Yorkers to have a greater impact on their elections. Our mission is to make local democracy more open, transparent, and equitable by removing barriers to participation.   We make it easier for New Yorkers to vote, meaningfully support candidates for city office, and run for office themselves. NYC Votes, our voter engagement initiative, meets people where they are to share trustworthy election information and help New Yorkers make a plan to vote. We publish the citywide Voter Guide, which delivers information about candidates directly to voters’ doors. Our public matching funds program ensures small contributions can make a big difference, allowing regular people to run for office by relying on the support of other regular people, not just wealthy donors and special interests. And we lift the veil on how candidates raise and spend money, increasing transparency and accountability in local government.   We believe that when every New Yorker is empowered to participate meaningfully in elections, candidates will better reflect the communities they serve, elected leaders will be more accountable to the public, and New Yorkers will have a democracy they can truly trust.   ABOUT THE UNIT   Strategy, Products, and Innovation Division    The Strategy, Products, and Innovation (SPI) division is where the agency plans its future and builds it. SPI brings together long-term planning, research and policy implementation, product development, and technology modernization operating across the agency to test new ideas and turn them into lasting improvements and new experiences. Across all of its work, the division is committed to advancing a democracy that is more open, transparent, and equitable for all New Yorkers.     Technology Department   The Technology Department builds, maintains, and secures the systems that make New York City’s campaign finance program work. This is the team behind CSMART, CFIS, FACTS, and the agency’s website, the platforms that power public matching funds, disclosure, and compliance for campaigns across the city. The department is in the middle of an ambitious modernization migrating core systems to the cloud, integrating modern software solutions where they fit, and building infrastructure engineered for the security, reliability, and scale that high-stakes public systems demand. Members of the team write and maintain custom software, strengthen the agency’s cybersecurity posture, and turn a legacy environment into a modern one. For engineers who want their work to matter, the mission of this team is to build the technology that makes democracy work better for all.     JOB DESCRIPTION    The New York City Campaign Finance Board seeks a Senior Director of Engineering to lead the engineering function that builds and runs the technology behind New York City's public matching funds program, the Voter Guide, and the agency's campaign finance disclosure and compliance systems. For engineers who want their work to matter, this is the seat that shapes how campaign finance, voter education, and public matching funds get built for the next decade of New York elections.   The platforms that power every city election are in the middle of a multi-year modernization from legacy .NET onto cloud-native Python infrastructure, targeting completion in 2027.   This senior leadership role owns the multi-year technical roadmap end to end, supervising software development, quality assurance, and Salesforce engineering, with data engineering operating as an agency-wide shared platform service that supports analytics and research teams across the agency. Within 6 to 12 months of hire, the role expands to include direct oversight of Infrastructure and Cybersecurity, consolidating engineering accountability across the agency's technical stack.   This is a turnaround leadership role. The Senior Director inherits a function with inconsistent engineering practice, meaningful technical debt, and technical leaders who are being tasked with growing their managerial capabilities. Building baseline engineering discipline, developing managerial capability, and delivering reliable services through active transformation are the core of the first two years.   This is also a build role. The Senior Director stands up a Salesforce engineering function from scratch, matures a data engineering operation into a shared platform service, and reskills a technical workforce alongside vendor knowledge transfer.   The role is designed for an engineering leader earlier in their leadership career, someone with the technical credibility to earn trust across engineering teams and the appetite to build practices where they do not yet exist.   Key Responsibilities   Leadership Development and Organizational Management     -  Build, supervise and mentor a leadership team across engineering functions (software development, quality assurance, Salesforce engineering, data engineering, and infrastructure), establishing clear accountability and developing managerial capability within the engineering organization.     -  Work with CFB leadership and internal partners to implement baseline people management practices, including hiring, performance management, career development, feedback, evaluation and retention strategies that attract and retain engineering talent in the public sector.     -  Foster an engineering culture that prioritizes collaborative problem-solving, knowledge-sharing, accountability, and continuous improvement across technical teams and agency-wide partnerships.                      -  In partnership with the Senior Director of Product, work with CFB leadership and internal partners to expand knowledge, engagement and comfort with the software development lifecycle, agile processes and product thinking, to ensure a balanced mixture of maintenance and stability, quality-of-life improvements and ambitious experimentation and innovation.   Strategic Technology Planning and Engineering Standards	     -  Set and track Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).     -  Develop and maintain a multiyear technical roadmap that aligns engineering work with the agency's product roadmap, digital priorities, and modernization goals.      -  Establish, document, and enforce engineering standards, including coding standards, branching strategy, security policies, compliance requirements, and architecture review practices.      -  Evaluate emerging technologies (including cloud-based solutions, open-source tools, and AI applications) and recommend adoption decisions appropriate to public-sector cost, risk, and capability constraints.   Software Development, QA, and AI Implementation Leadership     -  Develop and maintain a standard tracking system and reporting standards to track delivery flow, predictability, quality, and end-to-end traceability.       -  Lead the agency's software development and quality assurance functions, including supervision of engineering managers.      -  Own the software development lifecycle, DevOps, and CI/CD pipelines. Drive agile delivery practices in coordination with product leadership.      -  Own the technical implementation of AI use cases (building, integrating, and operating models in production as software delivery) and the technical evaluation of whether a model performs against the data provided (capability, accuracy, latency, cost, and technical security).      -  Manage technical debt proactively and make sound architecture decisions.   Infrastructure and Cybersecurity Oversight     -  Provide senior-level oversight of the agency's IT infrastructure and cybersecurity functions, including network architecture, cloud infrastructure, end-user computing, helpdesk operations, and the agency's cybersecurity posture.      -  Ensure alignment with citywide IT standards (NYC Office of Technology and Innovation) and cybersecurity requirements (NYC Cyber Command).      -  Lead disaster readiness and business continuity planning.   Data Engineering Build and Operations     -  Oversee the agency's data engineering build-and-operations function, delivering secure, scalable data infrastructure to enterprise governance standards.      -  Oversee design, construction, and operation of modern data architecture (the data lakehouse, real-time API integrations, and ETL/ELT pipelines).      -  Provide senior technical oversight of major data-architecture build decisions, including evaluating vendor-built data infrastructure for soundness and scalability.      -  Operate the function as an agency-wide shared platform service serving distributed analytics and research teams.   Salesforce Engineering Buildout     -  Build, from the ground up, an in-house Salesforce engineering function responsible for the codebase, configurations, documentation, and infrastructure of the agency's Salesforce instances.      -  Hire a Director of Salesforce Engineering and establish team structure, processes, and standards.      -  Establish in-house procedures for bug fixes, service requests, and feature enhancements.      -  Ensure Salesforce use aligns with NYC Cyber Command, internal security policy, and records retention requirements. ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES & OTHER BEHAVIORS (KSAOs)   We're seeking individuals eager to make an impact, even if they don't tick every box on our job description. Data Analyst II
Brex — São Paulo, São Paulo, Brazil

Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Data at Brex

The Data organization develops insights, models, and data infrastructure for teams across Brex, including Sales, Marketing, Product, Engineering, and Operations. Our Data Scientists, Analysts, and Engineers work together to make data—and insights derived from data—a core asset across the company.

What you’ll do

As a Data Analyst II (DA), you will play a central role in enhancing the operational tracking and reporting capabilities of different business teams across Brex. You will work closely with Data Scientists, Data Engineers, and partner teams to drive meaningful insights for the business through visualizations, self-service tools, and ad-hoc analyses. This is a high-impact role in a fast-paced fintech environment where your work will directly influence strategic decisions.

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in our São Paulo office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Responsibilities

- Apply data visualization and storytelling skills in creating business intelligence solutions (such as Looker and/or Hex dashboards) that enable actionable insights.

- Perform ad-hoc analyses and deep dives to investigate business questions, surface trends, and provide data-driven recommendations.

- Develop self-service data tools and processes that empower business stakeholders to independently monitor the performance and health of their respective areas.

- Collaborate closely with Data Scientists and Data Engineers to identify data sources, enable data pipelines, and support the development of analytical data models that operationalize reports and dashboards.

- Implement and maintain rigorous data quality checks to ensure the integrity and robustness of datasets used across dashboards, reports, and analyses.

- Partner with various departments—including Sales, Operations, Product, and Finance—to understand their data needs and deliver tailored analyses and reporting that support strategic planning.

- Contribute to the automation of recurring analyses and reporting workflows using Python.

Requirements

- 4+ years of experience in data analytics or a related role in a professional setting.

- 3+ years of experience working directly with Sales, Operations, Product, or equivalent business teams.

- Fluency in SQL to manipulate data and perform complex analyses (CTEs, window functions, joins across large datasets).

- Proficiency in Python for data analysis, automation, and scripting (Pandas, NumPy, and similar libraries).

- Experience with business intelligence and data visualization tools (Looker, Hex, Tableau, or similar).

- Strong quantitative and analytical skills with a demonstrated ability to translate data into business insights.

- Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with stakeholders across different functions and levels of technical fluency.

- Experience with generative AI and LLM-based tools (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot) to perform and accelerate analyses, automated reporting, and build self-service data tools.

Bonus points

- Familiarity with cloud data platforms (e.g., Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks).

- Familiarity with dbt for data modeling and transformation.

- Exposure to data pipeline orchestration tools (e.g., Airflow).

- Experience in fintech, financial services, or payments.

- Comfort operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with evolving priorities.

Brex LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary of Capital One, N.A.

TASK FORCE: 		Tax Policy, Revenue Forecasting and Economic Analysis  UNIT: 		         Property and Aggregate Revenue   JOB TITLE: 			One (1) Assistant Analyst / Analyst   CONTROL CODE: 	TAX-27-01   SUMMARY:  The Mayor’s Office of Management and Budget (OMB) is the City government's chief financial agency. OMB's staff of analysts and experts assembles and oversees the Mayor’s expense and capital budgets, which fund the services and activities of more than 90 City agencies and entities.    The Tax Policy, Forecasting and Economic Analysis Task Force is responsible for forecasting and monitoring trends in the local, national and global economies, including tax revenues, unemployment, and population growth.   Within this task force, the Tax Policy Unit monitors and forecasts revenues from City taxes, including real property tax, consumption taxes, personal income tax, business taxes and more. Annually, the City collects more than $80 billion in tax revenues. The property and aggregate revenue unit monitors and forecasts property and property related taxes amounting to over $34 billion and provides the reporting function of all the tax revenue collections.    JOB DESCRIPTION:  Tax policy analysis and revenue forecasting require thorough and up-to-date knowledge of the City’s economic structure as well as an understanding of the complex tax policy environment.   The duties of this position will encompass the following activities:  Data Organization/Maintenance: •	Maintain the current structure and accuracy of the taskforce’s SQL data systems using Python and Excel.  •	Standardize and/or expand data structures, and/or develop new data pipelines, and automate workflows. •	Facilitate regular review of data workflows for efficiency improvements. Data Reporting/Visualization: •	Maintain and/or improve current aggregate revenue reports and presentations using Python and Excel. •	Transform datasets into compelling visuals tailored for different levels of leadership and external government agencies using Python and Excel. •	Provide visual, technical, and editorial guidance to presentations as necessary. Tax Revenue Forecasting: •	Maintain current econometric forecast models for select property-related taxes such as the Commercial Rent Tax (CRT). •	Help with the organization and analysis of data related to the City’s Real Property Tax (RPT) system. Legislative and Policy Analysis: •	Track, interpret, and analyze local and state legislative tax proposals. •	Draft policy memos on legislative proposals, residential and commercial property tax incentives, and property-related revenue structures.  Taskforce Coordination: •	Facilitate cross-unit collaboration regarding the flow of data and information.  •	Communicate with external government agencies. Applicants should be well organized, able to multi-task, and have the capacity to understand a wide range of topics. This role can be fast paced at times and can require quickly digesting new information and developing informed opinions.  QUALIFICATIONS:  Hard Skills: •	Proficiency in Microsoft Office computer suite is required. •	Proficiency in STATA and Python, or other coding language with the ability to learn STATA and Python quickly. •	Experience working with, developing, or administering databases in SQL. •	Familiarity with economic forecasting tools such as linear regression, trend analysis, and out-of-sample prediction tests. •	A bachelor’s degree in economics or another quantitative subject. Soft Skills: •	Desire to work in and improve the functioning of the public sector.  •	Ability to effectively communicate within a team environment. •	Comfortable presenting to and sharing ideas with both internal and external teams. •	Able to maintain an open mind and provide creative solutions.  •	Strong analytic and quantitative skills. •	Detail-oriented and able to work with limited supervision. •	Availability to work late nights and weekends on a limited basis with advanced notice.  DESIRED SKILLS:  •	Familiarity with data science tools such as Azure Dev Ops, git, etc. •	Knowledge of economic policy evaluation tools such as difference-in-difference or regression discontinuity design. •	Comfortable working with large administrative datasets such as the American Community Survey Data.   REQUIREMENTS:  A cover letter is required to be considered for this position. Applications submitted without a cover letter will not be considered.  Assistant Analyst ($60,764+): Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Public Policy Analysis/Administration, or a subject related to the specific assignment with no full-time experience or one year of full-time experience in budgetary planning/management, financial analysis, public policy analysis/administration or a related field.  Analyst ($77,327): Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Public Policy Analysis/Administration, or a subject related to the specific assignment and a minimum of two years responsible budgetary planning/management, financial analysis, public policy analysis/administration or a related field; or an awarded Master's degree in Financial Management, Business, Public Administration or a field related to the specific assignment. You must be a City resident within 90 days of the date of appointment and you must be legally eligible to work in the United States.  SUBMISSION OF A RESUME IS NOT A GUARANTEE THAT YOU WILL RECEIVE AN INTERVIEW; ONLY THOSE CANDIDATES UNDER CONSIDERATION WILL BE CONTACTED. raw_text:
Commercial Counsel
Brex — New York, New York, United States

Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Legal at Brex

The Legal team helps the company grow responsibly, advocating for Brex and for the thousands of growing businesses we serve. We provide strategic advice and guidance to all Brex teams, protect Brex, advise on risk, and represent the company externally, negotiating with partners and interacting with regulators. Reimagining the financial system in a highly regulated environment requires creativity and resourcefulness, and we welcome the challenge.

What you’ll do

As Commercial Counsel at Brex, you will be an integral and versatile member of the Legal team and will support all aspects of the Company's commercial legal efforts. You will handle legal review and negotiation of Brex customer contracts, working closely with sales and other revenue-supporting teams to close deals efficiently while protecting the Company's interests. You'll also support vendor and partner contracting, negotiating a range of contracts that serve teams and departments across Brex. You will advise on legal issues that intersect with commercial matters, and collaborate with a wide range of cross-functional partners, including deal desk, ops, procurement, privacy, security, marketing, and people. You will contribute to the development and implementation of commercial legal resources and processes, including internal policies and procedures and contracting workflows. You'll provide sound and pragmatic legal advice and take a business-oriented approach to problem solving!

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in our New York City office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Responsibilities

- Draft, review, and negotiate customer agreements, from initial legal review through final signature, in partnership with sales, deal desk, and other stakeholders.

- Support the legal review and negotiation of a wide variety of inbound commercial contracts, including AI, SaaS, and other technology agreements, master and professional services agreements, consulting agreements, marketing, agency, and media contracts, event agreements, and non-disclosure agreements.

- Drive continuous improvement in commercial contracting processes, including developing and refining contracting playbooks, internal policies and procedures, and leveraging and optimizing AI contracting tools and contract lifecycle management (CLM) workflows.

- Identify and mitigate contractual risks within established parameters, escalating complex issues to SMEs and senior legal team members as needed.

- Provide sound, business-oriented legal advice to cross-functional partners on contract terms, deal structures, and commercial legal risks and opportunities.

- Collaborate closely with internal stakeholders to understand business needs, contextualize transactions, and translate business, operational and product requirements into clear legal terms and conditions.

- Be a business partner, not just an attorney!

Requirements

- Entrepreneurial mindset and comfort with taking ownership and acting upon it; you welcome challenges and thrive in dynamic, fast-paced environments!

- Minimum of 3-5 years of relevant experience practicing commercial law, either in-house at a technology company or within the corporate/tech transactions department of a reputable law firm. Experience at fast-paced growing technology companies is preferred.

- Juris Doctor (JD) and active bar membership in good standing in at least one US jurisdiction.

- Demonstrated experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating complex technology and commercial contracts; experience with both customer-facing and vendor/inbound contracting is ideal.

- Exceptional judgment, attention to detail, and integrity, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

- You are a builder, motivated by the continuous development and improvement of internal processes and resources. 

- Flexible, adaptive, and always open to learning something new.

Bonus Points

- Fintech or financial services experience, or familiarity with fintech product structures.

- Working knowledge of privacy issues in a commercial context. 

- Experience working directly with a deal desk team.

- Experience working with AI contracting tools or contract lifecycle management (CLM) technology.

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $220,000-$270,000 USD. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors, including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

Brex LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary of Capital One, N.A.
Please be aware, job-seekers may be at risk of targeting by malicious actors looking for personal data. Brex recruiters will only reach out via LinkedIn or email with a brex.com domain. Any outreach claiming to be from Brex via other sources should be ignored.
